event: At first light the moon orchids fold shut one by one, and the glasshouse goes green and plain.
Elsie wakes on the crate with her head on Tilly's shoulder; Tilly has held still all night.
Tamsin wakes on the cot with Margery's haft printed on her cheek.
Cora stands at the door, ledger shut, as straight as she stood at midnight.
The old grower comes down with a lamp and counts her orchids: every bloom whole.
She pays them the notice, and Elsie, Tamsin and Tilly share it evenly.
She gives Elsie a single closed moon orchid in a pot, for the moths she carried out.
Elsie holds the pot like a baby and says she will name it.
They walk back along the lake road as the sun comes up over the Mere.
Tilly yawns so wide her jaw clicks, and Tamsin carries her vials for her.
Elsie names the orchid Moonpenny out loud, and Cora repeats it under her breath.
At the Honeycomb Elsie runs up to set Moonpenny among her plants, and runs down again.
At the guild hall the clerk marks the orchid watch done, and frowns at his ledger.
He says Elsie and Tilly are one notice short of E-rank.
Tilly grabs Elsie's arm; Tamsin whoops so loud the whole hall turns.
New on the F-rank board: wash Brightwater Canal's lanterns, and a ring lost off the Lantern Steps.
Elsie picks the ring, because somebody must be so sad about it.
The clerk enters the party for the ring, and Cora writes it in her ledger.
At the Lantern Steps a young woman sits on the bottom step with her face in her hands.
She says it was her mother's ring, and she meant to give it to her sweetheart tonight.
She says it slipped off her finger and went in right there, by the third mooring post.
The water by the post is green and deep, with mud at the bottom.
Tamsin strips to her shift and dives in before anyone can talk about it.
She comes up blowing, with a fistful of mud and an old boot.
Tilly mixes two vials into her small steady blue flame and stoppers it tight.
She lowers the glowing vial on a string, and the bottom lights up blue.
Elsie pulls off her boots, ties up her skirt and goes down the slimy steps into the water.
The Mere is cold to her waist, and Cora says her name sharply from the top step.
Elsie ducks under, eyes open, and sees something glint by the post in the blue light.
She comes up gasping with the ring in her fist and holds it high.
The young woman bursts into tears and hugs Elsie, soaking herself through.
She pays them the notice; Elsie, Tamsin and Tilly share it, and Elsie gives Tilly the odd pips.
She says her sweetheart is Mira, and they'll both be at Lantern Night; Elsie says so will they.
Elsie climbs the steps streaming, and Cora takes off her charcoal coat and puts it round her.
Cora's coat is warm and smells of ink and lavender, and Elsie burrows into it.
Cora stands on the Lantern Steps in her shirtsleeves, and people stare at a Warden without her coat.
Tamsin, dripping, shakes her curls over Tilly, and Tilly shrieks.
Elsie wrings out Tamsin's curls with both hands, and Tamsin stands very still under them.
Back at the guild hall, damp, they hand the ring notice in at the clerk's desk.
The clerk takes Elsie's copper tag and Tilly's, and restamps each with an E.
Elsie holds her tag up to the window, and her eyes fill.
Tilly says the College only ever threw her out of things, and starts to cry too.
Tamsin hugs them both at once and lifts them off the floor.
Cora says congratulations, very formally, and holds out her hand.
Elsie hugs her instead, still wrapped in her coat, and Cora's ledger falls on the floor.
Tamsin picks up the ledger and hands it back with her eyes turned away, and Cora thanks her.
Elsie gives Cora her coat back, warm, and Cora buttons it to the throat.
Tamsin takes them to the E-rank board and taps the troll notice.
Two river trolls under an old toll bridge on the River Wend, taking sheep.
Tilly asks how big a troll is; Tamsin says big, and slow, and they sleep by day.
Elsie asks whether the trolls are hungry or just thieves, and nobody can say.
The clerk enters the party for the trolls, and Cora writes it in; they leave at dawn.
Cora says she will write to the guildmaster about the rank, and goes to the charcoal door.
Tamsin says they need sleep before trolls; Tilly says she needs a bath first.
Tilly goes off to Pickle Row to sleep, hugging Elsie twice at the corner.
Tamsin walks Elsie home and says she'll be at the Honeycomb door at dawn.
At the Honeycomb door Tamsin flicks Elsie's E tag with a finger and grins, and goes.
In the attic Elsie hangs her wet skirt at the window and puts on her other one.
Moonpenny sits among the other plants, and Elsie introduces her to each of them.
She sleeps till mid-afternoon with her E tag in her hand.
She goes down, and the baker sees the tag and says: well, now.
The baker gives her a honey bun and waves her coin away.
At the bakery table Elsie writes to her mother: E-rank, a ring in the Mere, a moon orchid.
After closing she borrows the ovens, and pays the baker for the firewood.
She bakes a honey cake for Lantern Night on her own, from her notebook.
The baker reads the notebook over her shoulder and corrects one word.
The cake goes under its cloth to rest, and Elsie licks the spoon.
From the round window she sees Cora walking alone along Thimble Canal.
Elsie waves with both arms; Cora stops, looks up, and after a moment lifts one hand.
Cora stands on the bridge a while looking up at the window, then walks on.
Down the Tether Tamsin is wide awake and fizzing, thinking of trolls.
Elsie hums down the thread until Tamsin's restlessness smooths out.
She sets her boots, salve and bandages by the door for the trolls.
The baker taps at the attic door to say the cake smells right, and goes down again.
